To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
RuCl(2)(PPh(3))(2) and AgOTf are an effective catalyst system for the cyclization of arenes and enes via intramolecular hydroarylation.

a new catalyst for hydroarylation of arene-ene compounds, RuCl(3) in the presence of silver triflate, has been developed and that this catalyst is effective for the cyclization of a variety of substrates.
RuCl(2)/AgOTf is a catalyst for the cyclization of arenes bearing a pendant alkene, and that this cyclization proceeds via a novel mechanism involving a cationic ruthenium species.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new catalytic methodologies for the formation of carbon-carbon bonds.
the synthesis of complex organic molecules by the use of transition metal catalysts.
the development of new catalytic processes that provide access to a variety of structurally diverse heterocyclic systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the Ru-catalyzed hydroarylation reaction is a reliable and efficient method for the construction of C-C bonds in a variety of substrates, and the method can be used for the synthesis of complex natural products and biologically active compounds.
RuCl3/AgOTf is an excellent catalyst system for the cyclization of arenes bearing an alkene moiety.
Ru(III) is a viable catalyst for the hydroarylation of arene-ene compounds, and the reaction is a viable alternative for the construction of heterocycles.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

RuCl3/AgOTf catalyzes a wide range of cyclizations of arene-ene systems, including the synthesis of a variety of terpenoids.
